83	## 3. Why the design is shaped this way
84	
85	- **Backend: self-hosted Sentry replaces Bugsink.** It gives replay, feedback, and error linking. The current client (`instrumentation-client.ts`) points at a Bugsink DSN with `integrations: []`, because Bugsink supports no integrations.
86	- **Recorder: our own rrweb, not Sentry's `replayIntegration`.** From the installed SDK source (`@sentry-internal/replay/build/npm/esm/index.js`):
87	  - buffer mode forces `checkoutEveryNms: BUFFER_CHECKOUT_TIME` (60000) and clears the buffer at every checkout, so it holds 0–60 s, and no option extends it;
88	  - `beforeAddRecordingEvent` only sees custom events (type 5), never DOM events, and `maskFn` is synchronous;
89	  - the buffer is append-only compressed in a worker, so there is nothing to preview or edit;
90	  - opening the feedback widget, `sendFeedback` (default `includeReplay: true`), and any `replaysOnErrorSampleRate > 0` all upload the replay without asking.
91	- **Upload: hand-built replay envelopes through Sentry's transport.** The replay envelope format is a published stable spec (v1.3.0, develop.sentry.dev/sdk/telemetry/replays), and Sentry's mobile SDKs build it themselves. Public `@sentry/core` exports (`createEnvelope`, `createEventEnvelopeHeaders`, `prepareEvent`, `uuid4`) plus `client.getTransport().send()` are enough. The recorder is `@sentry-internal/rrweb@2.35.0`, the fork Sentry's replay player uses.
92	- **Redaction: schema-driven tainting, a model only if needed.** Every column, RPC result, and edge-function payload gets a privacy classification. Values from classified sources are tainted as they reach the browser, and the redaction pass removes them from recorded text. Components rendering free text or grades are blocked outright. Sentry's server-side scrubbing only matches patterns (emails, IDs), so it is a backstop.

96	## 4. Decisions (ADRs, all final)
97	
98	1. **Retention: 30 days after the class ends.** A daily purge job (package 6b) deletes feedback and replays tagged with a `class_id` whose `classes.end_date` + 30 days has passed. Sentry's global `sentry.cleanup.days` (~150, human-owned) is the backstop, including for reports without a class.
99	2. **Who sees reports:** only platform admins and developers have Sentry access. Instructors don't get Sentry accounts. (A Pawtograder-side status view for instructors is out of scope for this handoff.)
100	3. **Identity:** reports and all Sentry events carry the Pawtograder user ID and role only, never name or email. This includes removing email from `Sentry.setUser` in `utils/supabase/middleware.ts` (~line 59; there is another `setUser` ~line 10). The report form has a "You may contact me about this" checkbox, sent as tag `contact_ok`. Staff look the user up by ID.
101	4. **Off by default:** the recorder is off unless the course flag is on and the route is listed (ADR 5). With the flag off, rrweb is not even loaded, but "Report a bug" still opens the dialog and files feedback without a replay. Where recording is on, the dialog shows a one-line notice ("This report includes a redacted recording of your last few minutes on this page").
102	5. **Route policy: off unless listed.** Two levels: `full` (masked text plus the unmask allowlist) and `structure` (every text node masked, no unmask). Pages that show a whole class (gradebook, submission review, rubric grading, roster, groups) are `structure` at most. Server-rendered pages that don't hydrate a `TableController` may be listed only with a taint block (section 4.3).
103	6. **Unmask governance:** a component unmasks text only by carrying `data-report-unmask`. CI requires CODEOWNERS review for any diff adding that attribute (grep check), and the lint rule (package 4b) plus leak test D15 check that no classified value reaches an unmasked component.
104	7. **Model or no model:** decided by package 4's go/no-go. Record the numbers either way.
105	8. **Owning the upload format:** pin `@sentry/*` and `@sentry-internal/rrweb` (and the player) to exact versions, group them in Renovate, and gate upgrades on the release-tier tests.
106	9. **Triage:** reports stay in Sentry. A weekly human triage promotes real bugs to GitHub issues linking to the Sentry item. Replays never go to GitHub.
107	10. **Schema-driven classification** as in section 3, generated by the E2E taint trace (package 2a) and approved by a human (HU6).

140	
141	`lib/bugReport/privacy.ts`:
142	
143	```ts
144	export type PiiKind = "name" | "email" | "handle" | "grade" | "free_text" | "none";
145	/** Every column of every table and view in public schema, key "table.column". */
146	export const COLUMNS: Record<string, PiiKind>;
147	/** RPCs: a kind for scalar/SETOF returns, or JSONPath → kind for custom/Json returns. */
148	export const RPCS: Record<string, PiiKind | Record<string, PiiKind>>;   // e.g. "$[*].students[*].name": "name"

154	- SETOF RPCs returning table rows map to that table's `COLUMNS`.

165	### 4.4 Tunnel
166	
167	- `app/api/tunnel/route.ts` must read the body as bytes: `arrayBuffer()`, split at the first `\n` to read the envelope header.
168	- It forwards only to the host and project ID parsed from `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`, returning 403 for anything else. This replaces `NEXT_PUBLIC_BUGSINK_HOST`.

173	## 5. Architecture
174	
175	```
176	browser, main thread
177	  recorder: @sentry-internal/rrweb record() (DOM observation must be on the main thread)
178	    checkoutEveryNms 60 s; ring of checkout segments; keep last 10 min; cap 20 MB of event JSON
179	    privacy at record time: maskAllText, maskAllInputs, block media/editors/avatars/[data-report-block],
180	      unmask only [data-report-unmask] (level "full" only), slimDOMOptions "all", inlineImages false
181	    type-5 breadcrumbs {tag:"breadcrumb", payload} for console, clicks, fetch (URL, method, status, duration; no bodies)
182	  taint set: filled from 5 ingest points (package 2) while recording is on; lasts one page load
183	  error linking: client.on("createDsc") adds replay_id; an event processor collects error_ids, trace_ids
184	
185	  user clicks Report → buffer frozen (copy), recording continues
186	
187	web worker
188	  redaction walker: FullSnapshot text, mutation texts/adds/attributes, input events, custom payloads
189	    detectors: taint set (Aho-Corasick) → regex backstop → model (only if package 4 ships)
190	  optional: segment storage and compression, if main-thread cost is visible (package 1 measures)
191	
192	review dialog (Chakra): @sentry-internal/rrweb-player on redacted events, remaining-strings list,
193	  click-to-redact (re-runs walker), keep-last-N-minutes control, description, contact checkbox, notice
194	
195	submit (the only upload):
196	  replay_event + replay_recording envelopes, segment 0..n, ≤ 8 MiB compressed each, sequential,
197	  via client.getTransport() → /api/tunnel → Sentry
198	  then Sentry.sendFeedback({message}, {includeReplay:false}) with contexts.feedback.replay_id set
199	```

314	  - `prepareEvent` a `replay_event` with `replay_id` = `event_id` = one fresh `uuid4()`, `segment_id` 0..n, `replay_type: "buffer"`, `replay_start_timestamp` (first kept event), `timestamp`, `urls`, `error_ids`, `trace_ids`;
315	  - body = `{"segment_id":n}\n` + zlib-compressed JSON of the events (`CompressionStream("deflate")`);
316	  - `createEnvelope` with both items; send sequentially via `client.getTransport().send()`.
317	- Segment 0 starts with Meta + FullSnapshot, and each segment is ≤ 8 MiB compressed.
318	- **Retries:** exponential backoff for 5xx and network errors, up to 3 tries per segment. A 429 aborts and shows "try again later".
319	- After all segments succeed, call `Sentry.sendFeedback({message}, {includeReplay: false})`, with `contexts.feedback.replay_id` set in a `beforeSendFeedback` hook. If the replay upload finally fails, still send feedback, without a `replay_id`, noting that the replay failed.
320	- Tags on the feedback and every replay event: `class_id`, `role`, `route` (pattern, not concrete path), `release`, `contact_ok`.
321	- **Tests:** F1, F2, F5, F6 (PR tier); F7, F8 (nightly and release tiers, pending HU2).
322	
323	### Package 6b: retention purge job
324	- A Supabase edge function `bug-report-retention-purge`, scheduled daily with `pg_cron`; see existing `cron.schedule` usage in `supabase/migrations/` for the pattern.
325	- For each class with `classes.end_date + 30 days < now()`, it deletes Sentry feedback and replays tagged with that `class_id` via the Sentry API, using `SENTRY_PURGE_TOKEN` (HU3).
326	- Each run logs counts only, no IDs or content.
327	- The first step is to confirm that the Sentry 26.5 API endpoints for deleting replays and feedback exist. If they don't, stop and report.
328	- **Tests:** H1–H3 (nightly, pending HU3).
329	
330	### Package 9: CI tiers
331	- **PR tier:** add the bug-reporter specs to the existing E2E jobs (see `.github/workflows/lint.yml`), with the fake tunnel fixture.
332	- **Nightly workflow:** `bug-reporter-nightly.yml`. Scheduled, plus PRs labeled `bug-reporter-full`. Full build profile, with the real dev Sentry through the secrets from HU2. Runs F7, F8, H, I, K.
333	- **Release workflow:** runs the release-tier tests on `@sentry/*` or rrweb version bumps (Renovate group) and before promoting staging to main.

335	### Packages 7 and 8

347	| **Nightly** | schedule, and PRs labeled `bug-reporter-full` | real `pawtograder-dev` | full profile |

# Bug reporter with redacted replay: implementation handoff

**For the implementing agent.** This file is self-contained: it is the whole spec, the decisions, and the test plan. Read it end to end before writing code. When this file and anything else disagree, this file wins; when this file is silent or ambiguous, stop and ask the human rather than guessing.

- Repository: `pawtograder/platform` (Next.js 15 + Supabase). Spec written against commit `329c3d8c` (Sep 27, 2026). Paths and line numbers below are from that commit; if a line has moved, search for the symbol.
- Installed SDK at that commit: `@sentry/*` and `@sentry-internal/*` 10.3.0.
- Written 2026-09-28. Status: all decisions final except the two open questions at the end.

---

## 1. Working agreement

### 1.1 Environment

- Set up the local stack by following `docs/local-dev.md` in the repo (Supabase CLI, `npx supabase db reset`, `npm run seed`, `npm run client-local` after any migration).
- The human provides these environment variables on your VM. **Never print, log, echo, or commit their values**, and never paste them into PR text, issues, or test output. Load them with `set -a; . <file the human names>; set +a`.

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `SENTRY_URL` | Base URL of the dev Sentry (self-hosted, Sentry 26.5.0) |
| `SENTRY_ORG` | `pawtograder-dev` |
| `SENTRY_PROJECT` | `pawtograder-web` (browser + Next server) |
| `SENTRY_PROJECT_EDGE` | `pawtograder-edge` (Supabase edge functions) |
| `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` | Agent token. Scopes: `org:read project:read project:releases event:read event:write`. It can read issues, events, replays, and feedback, upload source maps, and resolve issues. It cannot change settings, members, or delete data |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` | DSN for `pawtograder-web` |
| `SENTRY_DSN_EDGE` | DSN for `pawtograder-edge` |

- Use the Sentry web API (`$SENTRY_URL/api/0/...`, header `Authorization: Bearer $SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`) to verify what landed. You have no cluster access and must not need it.
- If a smoke event you send doesn't appear in Sentry within 60 s, stop and tell the human: that is an infrastructure fault (seen before: relay accepting events but not forwarding them), not a product bug.
- Use **synthetic data only**: the seed scripts and the canary seed (package 2a). Never point any of this at a real class.

### 1.2 Branches, PRs, done

- Base branch: `staging` (the repo default). One branch per work package, named `bug-reporter/pkg-<N>-<slug>` (e.g., `bug-reporter/pkg-0-sentry-switch`). Stack branches when a package depends on an unmerged one, and say so in the PR.
- Open a **draft PR** per package, titled `bug-reporter: pkg <N> - <summary>`. The description lists: the test IDs from section 7 that the PR makes pass, the measurements the package asks for, and anything you deferred. **Do not merge.** The human reviews and merges.
- **Done** for a package means: CI green; the package's listed test IDs pass in the tier stated; its acceptance items met; measurements recorded in the PR; no new lint warnings apart from the package 4b ratchet baseline.
- Keep everything user-visible behind the course flag (section 4.1). With the flag off, the product must behave exactly as before, except the package 0 Sentry switch and the report dialog without replay (ADR 4).

### 1.3 Never

- Add Sentry's `replayIntegration` or the feedback widget (`feedbackIntegration` with `autoInject`), or set `replaysSessionSampleRate` / `replaysOnErrorSampleRate` above 0. Section 3 explains why; test B5 enforces it.
- Upload anything replay-related before the user presses Submit.
- Unmask text, or remove a block, to make debugging easier.
- Add imports to `instrumentation-client.ts` beyond what package 0 needs. Its own comment warns that a bad import there silently takes Sentry and PostHog init down.
- Send a user's name or email to Sentry.

### 1.4 Human-owned tasks (not yours; mention in the PR if you're blocked on one)

| ID | Task | Blocks |
|---|---|---|
| HU1 | Rename the Sentry env vars in the staging deployment secrets and deploy staging | Package 0 staging acceptance |
| HU2 | Create CI secrets for the nightly and release tiers (`SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`) | Package 9 |
| HU3 | Create a delete-scoped `purge-dev` token and a `SENTRY_PURGE_TOKEN` secret | Package 6b acceptance, tests H1–H3 |
| HU4 | Prod Sentry deployment (package 7) | Enabling the flag for real students |
| HU5 | Check with the Khoury privacy contact before enabling for students | Enabling the flag for real students |
| HU6 | Review and approve the generated privacy classification (package 2a output) | Merging package 2 |

---

## 2. Problem and goal

"Report a bug" in `app/course/[course_id]/UserMenu.tsx` (~line 160) links to a GitHub issue template. Reports arrive without steps, route, release, or error. `app/global-error.tsx` has a Sentry event ID but offers only the same GitHub link, and `app/error/page.tsx` says "TODO file a bug report".

**Goal:** a user who hits a problem clicks **Report a bug**, watches a redacted replay of their last few minutes, redacts anything else, adds a description, and submits. Staff open one Sentry feedback item with the replay, linked errors, breadcrumbs, release, route, and the user's role.

### Hard constraints

1. **Nothing replay-related leaves the browser until submit.** Recording lives in a rolling buffer on the device. No sampling, no auto-flush on error.
2. **Redaction runs in the browser, before review, and may be async.** The user previews exactly what will be uploaded and can redact more.
3. **Our infrastructure only.** Self-hosted Sentry. Dev: the `pawtograder-dev` org. Prod: a separate install on the app's prod infrastructure (human-owned).
4. **Text masked by default.** Only components deliberately unmasked are recorded as text.
5. **Off by default for everything.** No course or route records unless explicitly turned on (section 4).
6. **Accessible review dialog.** Passes `assertStudentPageAccessible` (`tests/e2e/axeStudentA11y.ts`). The string list is the replay's text alternative.

### Non-goals

- Always-on session replay or analytics.
- Recording canvas, images, video, or code. Monaco and the markdown editor are blocked; there is no "attach my code" option in this version.
- A per-user opt-out setting. Control is per course and per route.

---

## 3. Why the design is shaped this way

- **Backend: self-hosted Sentry replaces Bugsink.** It gives replay, feedback, and error linking. The current client (`instrumentation-client.ts`) points at a Bugsink DSN with `integrations: []`, because Bugsink supports no integrations.
- **Recorder: our own rrweb, not Sentry's `replayIntegration`.** From the installed SDK source (`@sentry-internal/replay/build/npm/esm/index.js`):
  - buffer mode forces `checkoutEveryNms: BUFFER_CHECKOUT_TIME` (60000) and clears the buffer at every checkout, so it holds 0–60 s, and no option extends it;
  - `beforeAddRecordingEvent` only sees custom events (type 5), never DOM events, and `maskFn` is synchronous;
  - the buffer is append-only compressed in a worker, so there is nothing to preview or edit;
  - opening the feedback widget, `sendFeedback` (default `includeReplay: true`), and any `replaysOnErrorSampleRate > 0` all upload the replay without asking.
- **Upload: hand-built replay envelopes through Sentry's transport.** The replay envelope format is a published stable spec (v1.3.0, develop.sentry.dev/sdk/telemetry/replays), and Sentry's mobile SDKs build it themselves. Public `@sentry/core` exports (`createEnvelope`, `createEventEnvelopeHeaders`, `prepareEvent`, `uuid4`) plus `client.getTransport().send()` are enough. The recorder is `@sentry-internal/rrweb@2.35.0`, the fork Sentry's replay player uses.
- **Redaction: schema-driven tainting, a model only if needed.** Every column, RPC result, and edge-function payload gets a privacy classification. Values from classified sources are tainted as they reach the browser, and the redaction pass removes them from recorded text. Components rendering free text or grades are blocked outright. Sentry's server-side scrubbing only matches patterns (emails, IDs), so it is a backstop.

---

## 4. Decisions (ADRs, all final)

1. **Retention: 30 days after the class ends.** A daily purge job (package 6b) deletes feedback and replays tagged with a `class_id` whose `classes.end_date` + 30 days has passed. Sentry's global `sentry.cleanup.days` (~150, human-owned) is the backstop, including for reports without a class.
2. **Who sees reports:** only platform admins and developers have Sentry access. Instructors don't get Sentry accounts. (A Pawtograder-side status view for instructors is out of scope for this handoff.)
3. **Identity:** reports and all Sentry events carry the Pawtograder user ID and role only, never name or email. This includes removing email from `Sentry.setUser` in `utils/supabase/middleware.ts` (~line 59; there is another `setUser` ~line 10). The report form has a "You may contact me about this" checkbox, sent as tag `contact_ok`. Staff look the user up by ID.
4. **Off by default:** the recorder is off unless the course flag is on and the route is listed (ADR 5). With the flag off, rrweb is not even loaded, but "Report a bug" still opens the dialog and files feedback without a replay. Where recording is on, the dialog shows a one-line notice ("This report includes a redacted recording of your last few minutes on this page").
5. **Route policy: off unless listed.** Two levels: `full` (masked text plus the unmask allowlist) and `structure` (every text node masked, no unmask). Pages that show a whole class (gradebook, submission review, rubric grading, roster, groups) are `structure` at most. Server-rendered pages that don't hydrate a `TableController` may be listed only with a taint block (section 4.3).
6. **Unmask governance:** a component unmasks text only by carrying `data-report-unmask`. CI requires CODEOWNERS review for any diff adding that attribute (grep check), and the lint rule (package 4b) plus leak test D15 check that no classified value reaches an unmasked component.
7. **Model or no model:** decided by package 4's go/no-go. Record the numbers either way.
8. **Owning the upload format:** pin `@sentry/*` and `@sentry-internal/rrweb` (and the player) to exact versions, group them in Renovate, and gate upgrades on the release-tier tests.
9. **Triage:** reports stay in Sentry. A weekly human triage promotes real bugs to GitHub issues linking to the Sentry item. Replays never go to GitHub.
10. **Schema-driven classification** as in section 3, generated by the E2E taint trace (package 2a) and approved by a human (HU6).

### 4.1 Course flag

- Add `BUG_REPORT_RECORDING: "bug-report-recording"` to `COURSE_FEATURES` in `lib/courseFeatures.ts`, and a `MANAGEABLE_COURSE_FEATURES` entry so instructors can toggle it in course settings:
  - `defaultWhenMissing: false`, `navAffectsStaff: false`
  - `title: "Bug report recordings"`
  - `description: "When on, students and staff can attach a redacted recording of their last few minutes on supported pages when they report a bug. Nothing is uploaded unless they submit a report."`
  - `switchLabel` / `ariaLabel` in the style of the existing entries.
- Turning the flag off takes effect on the next navigation or page load: the recorder stops and discards its buffer (test A6). Live realtime propagation is not required.

### 4.2 Route policy file

`lib/bugReport/routePolicy.ts`:

```ts
export type RecordingLevel = "full" | "structure";
export type RoutePolicyEntry = {
  /** Next.js app-router pattern, e.g. "/course/[course_id]/assignments/[assignment_id]" */
  pattern: string;
  level: RecordingLevel;
  /** Required true for server-rendered pages that don't hydrate a TableController */
  ssrTaint?: boolean;
};
export const ROUTE_POLICY: readonly RoutePolicyEntry[] = [ /* start with a few student pages */ ];
export function recordingLevelFor(pathname: string): RecordingLevel | null; // null = don't record
```

- Matching: `[param]` matches one segment, `[...param]` matches the rest; the most specific pattern wins.
- Test override: when `process.env.E2E_ENABLE` is set, `recordingLevelFor` also honors a JSON policy in `localStorage["bugReport.testRoutePolicy"]`. Never in production builds.
- A unit test fails if any entry whose page is a server component without a controller lacks `ssrTaint: true`, and if any `ssrTaint: true` page doesn't render the taint block.

### 4.3 Privacy classification and taint block

`lib/bugReport/privacy.ts`:

```ts
export type PiiKind = "name" | "email" | "handle" | "grade" | "free_text" | "none";
/** Every column of every table and view in public schema, key "table.column". */
export const COLUMNS: Record<string, PiiKind>;
/** RPCs: a kind for scalar/SETOF returns, or JSONPath → kind for custom/Json returns. */
export const RPCS: Record<string, PiiKind | Record<string, PiiKind>>;   // e.g. "$[*].students[*].name": "name"
/** Edge functions by wrapper name in lib/edgeFunctions.ts, JSONPath → kind. */
export const EDGE_FUNCTIONS: Record<string, Record<string, PiiKind>>;
```

- JSONPath subset: `$`, `.key`, `[*]`. Nothing else.
- SETOF RPCs returning table rows map to that table's `COLUMNS`.
- `none` must be explicit; there is no default.

Taint block, for server-rendered pages listed with `ssrTaint: true`. The server component renders `<ReportTaint values={...} />` only when the flag is on and the route is listed. It outputs:

```html
<script type="application/json" id="report-taint">{"v":1,"values":{"name":["..."],"email":["..."],"handle":["..."]}}</script>
```

The recorder reads it once at start and adds the values to the taint set.

### 4.4 Tunnel

- `app/api/tunnel/route.ts` must read the body as bytes: `arrayBuffer()`, split at the first `\n` to read the envelope header.
- It forwards only to the host and project ID parsed from `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`, returning 403 for anything else. This replaces `NEXT_PUBLIC_BUGSINK_HOST`.
- Edge functions send server-to-server with `SENTRY_DSN_EDGE` and never use the tunnel.

## 5. Architecture

```
browser, main thread
  recorder: @sentry-internal/rrweb record() (DOM observation must be on the main thread)
    checkoutEveryNms 60 s; ring of checkout segments; keep last 10 min; cap 20 MB of event JSON
    privacy at record time: maskAllText, maskAllInputs, block media/editors/avatars/[data-report-block],
      unmask only [data-report-unmask] (level "full" only), slimDOMOptions "all", inlineImages false
    type-5 breadcrumbs {tag:"breadcrumb", payload} for console, clicks, fetch (URL, method, status, duration; no bodies)
  taint set: filled from 5 ingest points (package 2) while recording is on; lasts one page load
  error linking: client.on("createDsc") adds replay_id; an event processor collects error_ids, trace_ids

  user clicks Report → buffer frozen (copy), recording continues

web worker
  redaction walker: FullSnapshot text, mutation texts/adds/attributes, input events, custom payloads
    detectors: taint set (Aho-Corasick) → regex backstop → model (only if package 4 ships)
  optional: segment storage and compression, if main-thread cost is visible (package 1 measures)

review dialog (Chakra): @sentry-internal/rrweb-player on redacted events, remaining-strings list,
  click-to-redact (re-runs walker), keep-last-N-minutes control, description, contact checkbox, notice

submit (the only upload):
  replay_event + replay_recording envelopes, segment 0..n, ≤ 8 MiB compressed each, sequential,
  via client.getTransport() → /api/tunnel → Sentry
  then Sentry.sendFeedback({message}, {includeReplay:false}) with contexts.feedback.replay_id set
```

### Package 6: envelope builder and submit

# AGENTS.md

## Cursor Cloud specific instructions

### Overview

Pawtograder is a Next.js 15 + Supabase course operations platform (autograder, hand-grading, office hours, Q&A, gradebook). The codebase is a single Next.js application backed by a local Supabase instance (PostgreSQL, Auth, Realtime, Storage, Edge Functions) running in Docker.

### Starting services

1. **Docker daemon**: `sudo dockerd &>/tmp/dockerd.log &` — wait a few seconds, then verify with `docker info`. If `docker` commands fail with `permission denied ... /var/run/docker.sock`, prefer the least-privilege fix:
   - Make sure the socket is group-owned by `docker` and add your user to that group, then re-load the group membership for the current shell:
     ```bash
     sudo chown root:docker /var/run/docker.sock
     sudo usermod -aG docker "$USER"
     newgrp docker   # or: log out and back in to pick up the new group
     ```
   - Only as a last-resort temporary workaround on an ephemeral Cloud Agent VM (where the user is already root-equivalent and there is no other tenant on the machine) you may run `sudo chmod 666 /var/run/docker.sock`. **Do not use this on shared or persistent hosts**: it grants every local user full Docker daemon access, which is equivalent to root on the host.
2. **Supabase — ALWAYS START FROM A FRESH DB, NEVER RESTORE A BACKUP**:
   - `npx supabase start` restores from the previously-saved docker volume by default. In a Cloud Agent VM that volume is typically stale (snapshotted at some older schema version) and will be missing dozens of newer migrations — tests then fail with errors like `column ... does not exist`, `no partition of relation "audit" found for row`, or `Could not find the '...' column ... in the schema cache`.
   - **Correct sequence (do this every time before E2E):**
     1. If Supabase is already running, stop it WITHOUT a backup: `npx supabase stop --no-backup` (this deletes the stale volume).
     2. Also delete any leftover project volumes just to be safe: `docker volume ls --filter label=com.supabase.cli.project=pawtograder-platform -q | xargs -r docker volume rm`.
     3. Start fresh: `npx supabase start` — this will run every migration in `supabase/migrations/` against an empty DB.
   - **Storage RLS policies & the Supabase CLI version (IMPORTANT — pinned to `2.105.0`)**: storage bucket policies (avatars, uploads, submission-files) live **inline** in their migrations as plain `CREATE POLICY ... ON storage.objects`; no post-start superuser step is needed. This requires the pinned CLI: `supabase` is pinned to `2.105.0` in `package.json` (matching `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`), and `npx supabase` resolves that local devDep — don't run a globally-installed older CLI. On **older CLIs (e.g. 2.77.0)**, `supabase db reset` fails partway with `ERROR: must be owner of table objects` on the _later_ storage-policy migrations (e.g. `20260530120200`, `20260217000000`) while _earlier_ ones (avatars/uploads) succeed in the same run. Root cause is a race between the CLI's migration runner and the storage container re-owning `storage.objects` to `supabase_storage_admin` mid-reset — not the policy SQL itself (the same statement run interactively as `postgres` succeeds). CLI `2.105.0` applies all of them cleanly in both `supabase start` and `db reset`. If you hit `must be owner` on a fresh start, you're on the wrong CLI version — `rm -rf node_modules/.bin/supabase && npm install` (or `npm install supabase@2.105.0 -D`).
   - **Audit partitions**: The partitioned `public.audit` table only has partitions for a narrow date range out of migrations. If the current date is outside that range, inserts fail with `no partition of relation "audit" found for row`. After starting Supabase, run `docker exec -i supabase_db_pawtograder-platform psql -U postgres -d postgres -c "SELECT public.audit_maintain_partitions();"` to create today's partition (and the next 7 days).
   - **Sanity check the schema is current** before running E2E: the newest row of `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` should match the newest file under `supabase/migrations/` (e.g. `20260413234500`). If it doesn't, the DB was restored from a backup — redo the stop/restart-without-backup sequence above.
3. **Configure `.env.local`**: After `supabase start`, get keys with `npx supabase status -o env` and set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_URL`, and `ENABLE_SIGNUPS=true`.
   - There are **two modes** for `NEXT_PUBLIC_PAWTOGRADER_WEB_URL`. Pick one and keep it consistent across `.env.local`, the build step, and the test runner — mismatches cause silent magic-link / auth-redirect failures:
     - **Dev mode (port 3000)** — for `npm run dev` and iterative single-test runs via `npm run test:e2e:local`. Put `NEXT_PUBLIC_PAWTOGRADER_WEB_URL=http://localhost:3000` in `.env.local`. Playwright's `BASE_URL` defaults to `http://localhost:3000` in this mode.
     - **Prod E2E mode (port 3001)** — required for full-suite runs. Because Next.js **inlines `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` at build time**, you must `export NEXT_PUBLIC_PAWTOGRADER_WEB_URL=http://localhost:3001` _before_ `npm run build`. Exporting it only when running Playwright (or only in `.env.local` at runtime) does **not** update an already-built bundle. Keep the same value in `.env.local` while iterating (so `supabase functions serve` picks it up) and run the tests with `BASE_URL=http://localhost:3001 npx playwright test ...` and the prod server on `PORT=3001 npm run start`.
4. **Edge Functions (recommended for local E2E/prod-mode testing)**: `npx supabase functions serve --env-file .env.local` — serves local functions at `http://127.0.0.1:54321/functions/v1/*`.
   - Required when testing flows that invoke `autograder-create-submission`, `autograder-submit-feedback`, webhooks, or async workers.
5. **Next.js dev server (iterative dev only)**: `npm run dev` — serves at `http://localhost:3000`. Do NOT use `next dev` for E2E runs; use the prod build on port 3001 (see below). `next dev` is dramatically slower per-request and causes widespread Playwright timeouts during full-suite runs.

### Seeding the database

Run `npm run seed` to create a test class with students, assignments, and login credentials. The output includes instructor/grader/student emails (all with password `change-it`). The instructor dashboard is at `/course/<class_id>`.

### Before committing

**Always** run `npm run format` before committing. This runs Prettier on the entire codebase. CI will reject unformatted code.

### Lint / Test / Build

- **Lint**: `npm run lint` (ESLint + Prettier). See `package.json` scripts.
- **Unit tests**: `npm test` (Jest). Note: `jest.setup.ts` must exist (import `@testing-library/jest-dom`). The existing test has a pre-existing issue with `Request` not being defined in jsdom.
- **E2E — prod build (REQUIRED for full-suite runs)**: Always use a production build + `next start` for E2E, not `next dev`. `next dev` in this environment causes widespread Playwright timeouts across the full suite (first-hit compile cost on every route).
  - Never run `next dev` and `next start` at the same time. Stop all dev servers before prod E2E runs.
  - Export `NEXT_PUBLIC_PAWTOGRADER_WEB_URL` to match the prod server port **before** building — `npm run build` bakes the value into the bundle, and changing the env at runtime will not update an existing `.next` output. Re-export and rebuild from a clean `.next` directory whenever you switch modes: `export NEXT_PUBLIC_PAWTOGRADER_WEB_URL=http://localhost:3001 && rm -rf .next && npm run build`
  - Start only the prod server: `PORT=3001 npm run start`
  - Run Playwright with matching **`BASE_URL`**: `BASE_URL=http://localhost:3001 npx playwright test ...` (the **built** app URL comes from the build step above; Playwright only needs `BASE_URL` to match where `next start` listens).
- **E2E — dev-mode (only for rapid iteration on a single test)**: With local Supabase running and `npm run dev` (port 3000), run **`npm run test:e2e:local`** — it sets `BASE_URL=http://localhost:3000` to match the dev server (`playwright.config.ts`). Ensure **`SUPABASE_URL`**, **`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`**, and **`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`** are in `.env.local` or exported: `tests/e2e/TestingUtils.ts` loads `.env.local` via dotenv and uses those values (plus the service role for the admin client) for setup and auth helpers. Do not use this mode for running the whole suite.

   - Make sure the socket is group-owned by `docker` and add your user to that group, then re-load the group membership for the current shell:
     ```bash
     sudo chown root:docker /var/run/docker.sock
     sudo usermod -aG docker "$USER"
     newgrp docker   # or: log out and back in to pick up the new group
     ```
   - Only as a last-resort temporary workaround on an ephemeral Cloud Agent VM (where the user is already root-equivalent and there is no other tenant on the machine) you may run `sudo chmod 666 /var/run/docker.sock`. **Do not use this on shared or persistent hosts**: it grants every local user full Docker daemon access, which is equivalent to root on the host.
2. **Supabase — ALWAYS START FROM A FRESH DB, NEVER RESTORE A BACKUP**:
   - `npx supabase start` restores from the previously-saved docker volume by default. In a Cloud Agent VM that volume is typically stale (snapshotted at some older schema version) and will be missing dozens of newer migrations — tests then fail with errors like `column ... does not exist`, `no partition of relation "audit" found for row`, or `Could not find the '...' column ... in the schema cache`.

     1. If Supabase is already running, stop it WITHOUT a backup: `npx supabase stop --no-backup` (this deletes the stale volume).

     3. Start fresh: `npx supabase start` — this will run every migration in `supabase/migrations/` against an empty DB.

ON storage.objects`; no post-start superuser step is needed. Root cause is a race between the CLI's migration runner and the storage container re-owning `storage.objects` to `supabase_storage_admin` mid-reset — not the policy SQL itself (the same statement run interactively as `postgres` succeeds). CLI `2.105.0` applies all of them cleanly in both `supabase start` and `db reset`. # Writing rules for this project

<!-- maintainer: bump the version string below on every release; see README "Maintainer notes" -->

These rules apply to all prose in this repository. They were generated by `/ai-slop:init` from the [ai-slop-skill](https://github.com/se-uhd/ai-slop-skill) (skill version 2026-07) and combine the writing rules maintained by the [Software Engineering Group at Heidelberg University](https://github.com/se-uhd) with a general AI-trope catalog from [tropes.fyi](https://tropes.fyi) by [ossama.is](https://ossama.is).

Edit this file freely to add project-specific conventions. The sections below are a starting point; once you edit them, this file is yours.

To audit a draft against everything below, run `/ai-slop:review` (or `/ai-slop:review-diff` to scope the audit to git-modified lines).

## Language

- **Use American English consistently.** That means analyze (not analyse), behavior (not behaviour), organization (not organisation), modeling (not modelling), color (not colour). Check for British spellings introduced by collaborators or spell-checkers set to the wrong locale.
- **Treat "data" as singular.** "The data shows" and "the data is," not "the data show" or "the data are." Project convention: both forms are accepted in style guides, but we use singular consistently.
- **Use "such as" not "like" to introduce examples.** Write "scenarios such as code completion," not "scenarios like code completion." `Like` is colloquial in this construction; `such as` is the more formal register. <result>None of the three questions came out as a clean go. Open question 1 and the 6b precondition are go. Open question 2 is blocked by an infrastructure fault in the dev Sentry: it accepts replays but never stores them. The tool refused to write `REPORT.md`, so the full report is below. The scripts are in `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-jon-platform/8b39a430-78a7-4625-b584-fa0fd315d6ec/scratchpad/research/`.

## Verdicts

| Question | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **Open question 2** (`replay_type:"buffer"`, no triggering error, start 5 min ago) | **Blocked by the fault.** Every replay envelope got HTTP 200 with no rejection, so relay accepts the format. But no replay of any kind gets stored here, including a normal session-mode replay sent by the real `@sentry/browser` 10.3.0 SDK. So the failure isn't specific to our format, but ingest isn't confirmed either. Per the brief, I stopped after one run of each and didn't keep retrying. |
| **Open question 1** (per-item size limit) | **Go for the 8 MiB cap.** 8.0 MiB → 200, 9.9 MiB → 200, 10.5 MiB → **413** `envelope exceeded size limits for type 'replay_recording'`, logged by Sentry as `too_large:replay_recording`. The limit is 10 MiB on the whole item, including the `{"segment_id":n}\n` line. Package 6 should treat 413 as permanent: no retry. Whether the 8 MiB replay was *stored* can't be checked because of the fault. |
| **6b precondition** (delete endpoints) | **Go.** All the endpoints exist at tag 26.5.0 and return 403 (not 404/405) to the agent token. The HU3 purge token needs **`project:write`** for replays and **`event:admin`** for feedback. |
| Linked error | The error side works: it carries `tags.replayId` and `contexts.replay.replay_id`, and a Discover query `replayId:<id>` finds it. The replay side (`error_ids`, `count_errors`) can't be checked. |
| Feedback | **Works.** Visible via the API in 250 ms as a `feedback` issue with `class_id`, `role`, `route`, `release` and `contact_ok`. `contexts.feedback.replay_id` is set and Sentry adds `contexts.replay.replay_id` from it. Email and name are null. |

## Infrastructure fault (for the human)
- Seven replays got 200 but none can be found: details endpoint 404 after 90 s, replay list empty, `hasReplays: false`. These were 3 hand-built buffer segments, 1 hand-built session replay, 2 size-test replays and 1 from the real SDK.
- Sentry's usage stats record no outcome for any of the accepted replays, yet they do record the 10.5 MiB rejection. So relay passes replays on and they are lost afterwards. Sentry records a replay as accepted only when its replay consumer processes segment 0, so that consumer is probably not processing them.
- `GET /projects/{org}/{proj}/replays/<any id>/recording-segments/` returns an HTML 500 for every id, even random ones, in both projects. In 26.5.0 that endpoint starts by setting up the replay blob storage, so the storage setting (`replay.storage.backend`) is probably misconfigured.
- The org has the `session-replay` feature, so this isn't a feature flag.
- To check on the cluster: whether the `ingest-replay-recordings` consumer and the snuba replays consumer are running, whether the install uses the `errors-only` profile, and the replay storage config.
- Once fixed, `node send-replay.mjs && node verify-replay.mjs` answers open question 2 in about 2 minutes.

## Shapes that got 2xx
- **Endpoint:** built by `getEnvelopeEndpointWithUrlEncodedAuth(dsnFromString(dsn))`, sent through `@sentry/core` `createTransport` (the same transport code the browser SDK uses).
- **Replay segment:** a `replay_event` item plus a `replay_recording` item, the same shape the SDK's `createReplayEnvelope` builds.
  - The event has `event_id` = `replay_id`, `segment_id`, `replay_type`, `replay_start_timestamp`, `timestamp`, `urls`, `error_ids`, `trace_ids`, `tags`, `user:{id}` and `platform:"javascript"`.
  - The recording body is `{"segment_id":n}\n` followed by zlib deflate of the rrweb event array.
- **Linked error:** `contexts.replay.replay_id`, `tags.replayId`, a trace id that is listed in the replay's `trace_ids`, and the error's id in segment 0's `error_ids`.
- **Feedback:** item `{"type":"feedback"}` with `contexts.feedback {message, url, source:"api", replay_id, associated_event_id}`.

## API for F7 and the purge (base `/api/0`)

| Need | Request | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Replay details | `GET /organizations/{org}/replays/{id}/` | Returns `tags` (map of lists), `error_ids`, `trace_ids`, `count_segments`, `count_errors`, `user {id, username, email, ip, display_name}`, `urls`, `replay_type` |
| Download recording | `GET /projects/{org}/{proj}/replays/{id}/recording-segments/?per_page=100` | Always returns the bodies as JSON `[[seg0 events], ...]`, already inflated; currently 500 here |
| One segment | `…/recording-segments/{n}/?download` | Raw segment JSON |
| Replays by tag | `GET /organizations/{org}/replays/?project=-1&statsPeriod=90d&query=class_id:N` | 200 |
| Feedback by tag | `GET /organizations/{org}/issues/?project=-1&statsPeriod=90d&query=issue.category:feedback class_id:N` | Returns resolved items too once `query` is given. Searches that don't name `issue.category:feedback` leave feedback out. |
| Linked errors via Discover | `GET /organizations/{org}/events/?dataset=discover&field=id&query=replayId:<id>` | Found the linked error |
| Feedback event | `GET /projects/{org}/{proj}/events/{id}/` | |
| Delete one replay | `DELETE /projects/{org}/{proj}/replays/{id}/` | `project:write`. Async; returns 204 even for an id with no data |
| Bulk-delete replays by query | `POST /projects/{org}/{proj}/replays/jobs/delete/` with `{"data":{"rangeStart","rangeEnd","environments":[],"query":"class_id:N"}}` → 201 | `project:write`. Poll `GET …/jobs/delete/{job_id}/` for status |
| Delete feedback issues | `DELETE /organizations/{org}/issues/?id=…&id=…` → 204 | `event:admin`, at most 1000 per call, feedback issues qualify |
| Delete one issue | `DELETE /organizations/{org}/issues/{id}/` → 202 | `event:admin`, limited to 5 per 5 s |

For feedback, the purge job should list ids with the tag query and then delete by `?id=`: with ids given, the endpoint ignores the query, so a delete can't match more than intended.

## SDK checks (@sentry/core 10.3.0)
- **Binary items:** `serializeEnvelope` appends a `Uint8Array` payload unchanged. A round trip of random bytes and of a real recording containing `\n` bytes came back byte-identical (`check-serialize.mjs`).
- **Transport gotchas:**
  - If an earlier response rate-limited replays, `send()` quietly drops the items and returns `{}` with no `statusCode`, so package 6 must treat a missing status as failure.
  - For bodies of 60 KB or less the browser transport sets `keepalive`. That only happens at submit, but B3's "no keepalive" assertion needs to allow it there.
- **`sendFeedback(…, {includeReplay:false})`:** `includeReplay` is only read by `replayIntegration`, which we don't install, so replay code is never touched. Two side effects:
  - It calls `getCurrentScope().setTags(params.tags)`, which leaves `class_id`, `contact_ok` and the rest on every later error. Call it inside `withScope`, or set the tags in the hook instead.
  - It defaults `url` to `location.href`, the concrete path with ids, which becomes the `url` tag and `contexts.feedback.url`. Pass `url` explicitly if D17 wants only the route pattern.
- **`beforeSendFeedback`:**
  - It's a client hook (`client.on(...)`), not an init option.
  - It runs synchronously and gets the raw feedback event. It can change `contexts.feedback.replay_id`, `tags`, `user` and `contexts` in place.
  - It can't drop the event, async work in it isn't awaited, and the scope's data is merged in afterwards.
  - `beforeSend` does not run for feedback at all.

## Question for the human
The stored feedback has `user.ip_address` filled in with a private ingress IP. Sentry inferred it even though our events sent none. To keep reports to user ID and role (ADR 3), either send `ip_address: null` on replay events and feedback, or turn on the org's "Prevent storing of IP addresses". Which do you want?

## Cleanup
The 3 test issues are resolved (smoke error 156, linked error 158, feedback 157). A scan of the research directory for the Sentry URL, token, DSN host and DSN key found nothing.

## Files
In `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-jon-platform/8b39a430-78a7-4625-b584-fa0fd315d6ec/scratchpad/research/`. Run each from that directory after `set -a; . ~/.config/sentry-dev/pawtograder.env; set +a`.
- `lib.mjs`: shared helpers (transport, API client, synthetic rrweb events, envelope builder).
- `send-replay.mjs`: sends a linked error, then N segments, then feedback. Flags: `--segments`, `--start-minutes-ago`, `--replay-type`, `--no-error`, `--no-feedback`, `--class-id`, `--out`.
- `verify-replay.mjs`: the F7 checks against a run's ids.
- `smoke.mjs`: F8 smoke error; exits 2 if it isn't visible in 60 s.
- `size-test.mjs`: the size-limit probe; results in `size-test-results.json`.
- `probe-delete.mjs`: the non-destructive 6b probe; output in `probe-delete.log`.
- `check-serialize.mjs`: offline check of binary envelopes.
- `sdk-control.mjs`: diagnostic run of the real SDK in headless Chromium; needs `sdk-bundle.js` built from `sdk-entry.js` with esbuild.
- `resolve-test-issues.mjs`: resolves the research issues.
- `src/`: the Sentry 26.5.0 source files I read.</result>

## API (base /api/0)
- Replay details: GET /organizations/{org}/replays/{id}/ (tags, error_ids, trace_ids, count_segments, count_errors, user, urls, replay_type)
- Recording: GET /projects/{org}/{proj}/replays/{id}/recording-segments/?per_page=100 (inflated JSON [[seg0],...]); one segment: …/recording-segments/{n}/?download
- Replays by tag: GET /organizations/{org}/replays/?project=-1&statsPeriod=90d&query=class_id:N
- Feedback by tag: GET /organizations/{org}/issues/?project=-1&statsPeriod=90d&query=issue.category:feedback class_id:N
- Discover linked errors: GET /organizations/{org}/events/?dataset=discover&field=id&query=replayId:<id>

- Sentry infers user.ip_address (private ingress IP) even when none is sent. Open question to the human: send ip_address null, or turn on the org's "Prevent storing IP addresses".

content.text:
The research agent finished. What it found:

- **The dev Sentry drops replays (infrastructure fault).** Every replay envelope got HTTP 200, but none was stored, including one sent by the real `@sentry/browser` 10.3.0 SDK. The recording-segments endpoint returns HTTP 500 for every id. That points at the replay consumer or replay blob storage (`replay.storage.backend`) on the install. The spec says to stop and tell you about faults like this. It blocks F7 and the answer to open question 2. Once it's fixed, `node send-replay.mjs && node verify-replay.mjs` in `scratchpad/research/` answers question 2 in about 2 minutes. Error events and feedback arrive fine.
- **Open question 1 (size limit): go.** Replay recordings of 8.0 and 9.9 MiB were accepted; 10.5 MiB was rejected with HTTP 413. So the limit is 10 MiB per item and the spec's 8 MiB segment cap is safe.
- **Package 6b delete endpoints: go.** They exist in 26.5. The `SENTRY_PURGE_TOKEN` you create for HU3 needs `project:write` (replays) and `event:admin` (feedback).
- **Feedback works.** It shows up with all five tags and links to the replay id. Name and email are null.

**IP addresses:** Sentry fills in `user.ip_address` even when we send none. Unless you say otherwise, the code will send `ip_address: null` and stop Sentry inferring it on every event it builds. The org's "Prevent storing of IP addresses" setting is a server-side backstop you can also turn on; I'll mention it in the PR.

Six agents are running: package 0 (Sentry switch), 1 (recorder), 2 (privacy classification), 5 (report dialog), 6b (purge job), plus the finished research agent's report for later agents. The next steps are merging their branches into `feature/bug-reporter`, then the taint ingest points, the redaction worker, and the upload.

- `lib/bugReport/privacy.ts` is the draft classification, with a header saying it awaits HU6. Its types live in `lib/bugReport/privacyTypes.ts` and `privacy.ts` re-exports them.
- `lib/bugReport/selectParser.ts`, `variants.ts` and `regexBackstop.ts`.

  - `generatePrivacyDraft.ts`: by default it keeps existing entries and hand edits, adds `// DRAFT` entries for new keys and drops entries for removed keys. `--fresh` rebuilds everything and `--check` fails if the file is out of date.
  - `columnHeuristics.ts` (column-name rules), `privacyOverrides.ts` (hand decisions) and `rpcReturnReview.json` (return shapes of the 58 RPCs that return Json, text or a record, read from their SQL by three read-only subagents; I spot-checked the results rather than reviewing every one).

- `scripts/PostprocessSupabaseTypes.ts` now fails `client`/`client-local` when anything lacks an entry, names the missing keys, and tells you to run the generator. I checked this with an injected column.

**APIs the ingest phase and 2a build on**
- **`privacy.ts`** exports `PiiKind`, `TableRef = { $table }`, `JsonPathMap`, `RpcClassification`, `COLUMNS`, `RPCS` and `EDGE_FUNCTIONS`.
- **Table rows:** RPCs that return rows of a table are written `{ $table: "profiles" }`. The same marker can be the value of a JSONPath entry for rows embedded in Json.
- **Deviation from the spec:** the `RPCS` type is widened from the spec's `PiiKind | Record<string, PiiKind>` so it can hold that marker.
- **JSONPath rule:** the most specific path covering a value decides its kind, and a path to an object covers everything under it. A value no path covers is reported, never treated as `none`.
- **Edge functions:** wrappers that only call RPCs map `$` to `none`, and every wrapper maps `$.error` to `free_text`.
- **`selectParser.ts`** exports:
  - `classifyResponse(url, method, body)`, which returns `{ handled, values: {value, kind, source}[], unclassified }`
  - `classifyRows(relation, rows)`, for `TableController` data and realtime rows
  - `parseSelect` and `resolveEmbed`
- **`variants.ts`** exports `normalizeForMatch`, `nameVariants`, `personNameDisplay`, `personNameVariants`, `matchPatterns(value, kind)` and `MIN_MATCH_LENGTH = 3`. Grades, initials and strings under 3 characters produce nothing.
- **`regexBackstop.ts`** exports `findBackstopSpans(text)`, which returns sorted, merged `{start, end, kind: "email" | "nuid" | "mailto"}` spans. Package 3 still has to wrap it in its async detector interface.

**Counts**

| Section | Entries | By kind | Marked uncertain |
|---|---|---|---|
| Columns (153 tables, 15 views) | 1793 | none 1580, free_text 102, grade 46, handle 34, name 24, email 7 | 64 |
| RPCs | 326 | 50 carry PII or table rows; 7 table-row returns | 23 |
| Edge-function wrappers | 54 | 45 not all-`none`; 30 carry PII beyond `$.error` | 5 |

**Decisions for the human, flagged in the review guide**
1. **Staff-written course content is `none`:** assignment titles and descriptions, rubric text, section names. Changing it to `free_text` would block those components in replays.
2. **Json columns of unknown shape are `free_text`:** audit rows, GitHub payloads and the like. That taints enum strings such as "open" inside them, so the ingest phase may need to skip short or enum-like values. That is a product call.
3. **Extensions and late tokens are `grade`,** because they can reveal an accommodation.
4. **Repository names are `handle`,** because they embed the student's GitHub username.
5. **One RPC can't be fully expressed.** `get_gradebook_records_for_all_students_array` returns positional arrays with a free-text note at index 9, which the JSONPath subset can't address. The whole array is `grade`, so that note is protected only by blocking, never by matching.
6. **One edge function has no classification.** `submission-serve-artifact` is called directly from the submission files page (`files/page.tsx`), not through a wrapper in `lib/edgeFunctions.ts`. The parser reports its response as unclassified.

`npx tsc` shows errors only in two files I didn't touch: `tests/e2e/test-assignment-view-as-student.spec.ts` and `tests/unit/bulk-assign-assignee-options.test.ts`.</result>
